title: Dominic and the Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Quentin Whitlock is summoned to read the will of Edmund Voss, founder of the town of Halloway—who died forty years ago. The will, dated last spring and bearing his unmistakable signature, leaves everything to a stranger named Dominic Ashe, a man no one in town has ever met. When the town council forces an exhumation to settle the dispute, Voss's coffin proves empty, and Quentin realizes the founder may never have died at all—or that someone wanted the town to believe he had. Digging through sealed records and her own firm's compromised archives, Quentin discovers Dominic Ashe is the son Voss secretly fathered, hidden away to protect him from a decades-old crime that built Halloway's fortune: the disappearance of three mill workers whose deaths were ruled accidental. The empty coffin was staged by Voss himself before his real death, a final act meant to force the town—and Quentin, whose own family was complicit—to confront the buried truth. In the end, Quentin closes the case by proving the original deaths were murders, secures Dominic's inheritance, and chooses to stop hiding behind professional invisibility by publicly naming her grandfather among the guilty.
about_author: Rafael Marchetti is a former small-town archivist who spent years cataloguing probate records before turning to fiction, giving his mysteries an insider's feel for paper trails and quiet secrets. He lives in New England, where he writes stories about towns that remember more than they admit.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Quentin Whitlock, meticulous and deliberately unremarkable, opens a probate file for Edmund Voss—dead forty years—and finds a fresh will naming an unknown heir, Dominic Ashe. Her senior partner urges her to refuse it; her pride won't allow it. POV: Quentin. Beat: cold curiosity hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: A Town Built on One Name
chapters.summary: Quentin arrives in Halloway, where Voss's face is on the fountain, the school, the mill museum. Everyone she interviews offers identical, rehearsed praise. A librarian slips her a note: 'Ask about 1984.' POV: Quentin. Beat: unease beneath postcard surfaces.

chapters.title: Dominic
chapters.summary: Quentin tracks down Dominic Ashe, a guarded ferry mechanic in his fifties who claims he never contacted any lawyer and barely knows the name Voss. Yet he carries a locket with Voss's photograph. POV: alternating Quentin and Dominic. Beat: two strangers circling a shared lie.

chapters.title: Signature and Seal
chapters.summary: Back at the office, a document examiner confirms the signature is authentic—but the notary stamp belongs to a commission revoked in 1990. Someone with access to old firm materials forged around a genuine relic. POV: Quentin. Beat: the enemy is inside her own world.

chapters.title: The Council Objects
chapters.summary: Halloway's town council moves to void the will, led by the charming Harlan Pike, Voss's grand-nephew. They demand proof the testator is actually dead—forcing an exhumation Quentin privately dreads. POV: Quentin. Beat: pressure mounts from every respectable direction.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gave Back
chapters.summary: At dawn, before officials and gawkers, the coffin is opened: it holds weighted sandbags and a suit no one can identify. The crowd's murmur turns hungry. Quentin notices fresh disturbance marks in the grave soil—someone got there first, recently. POV: Quentin. Beat: shock, then dread.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Flowers
chapters.summary: Graveyard caretaker Mabel Dunn admits someone has tended the grave every week since 1984—always paying cash, always hooded. She kept one dropped receipt from a hardware store twenty miles away. POV: Mabel, then Quentin. Beat: grief disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Mill Ledgers
chapters.summary: In the historical society basement, Quentin finds gaps in the 1984 mill payroll: three workers erased mid-month, their accident reports signed by a young Quentin's grandfather, then the firm's junior partner. POV: Quentin. Beat: personal history curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Harlan's Offer
chapters.summary: Pike offers Quentin a lucrative retainer to declare the will invalid quietly, hinting he knows about her grandfather's signature. She declines, and that night her office is searched—nothing taken but the Voss file's photocopies. POV: Quentin. Beat: temptation refused, threat received.

chapters.title: Locket and Letter
chapters.summary: Dominic finally opens up: raised by a 'godmother' who died when he was nineteen, leaving him money, the locket, and instructions never to come to Halloway. He never knew why until now. POV: Dominic. Beat: abandonment reframed as protection.

chapters.title: The Godmother's House
chapters.summary: Quentin and Dominic search the godmother's preserved cottage and find letters from Voss spanning decades—affectionate, guilty, increasingly frightened after 1984. The last letter mentions 'the ledger under the bell.' POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness entangled with terror.

chapters.title: Under the Bell
chapters.summary: In the decommissioned mill, inside the old shift-bell housing, they recover a hidden ledger recording payments to the three workers' families—hush money drawn against company accounts, initialed by Voss and two partners. POV: Quentin. Beat: triumph shadowed by scale of the cover-up.

chapters.title: One Partner Still Breathing
chapters.summary: Of Voss's two partners, one died in 1991; the other, Aldous Crane, is Halloway's retired judge—the man who certified the 1984 accident rulings. Quentin realizes the exhumation order passed through his chambers. POV: Quentin. Beat: the circle tightens.

chapters.title: Empty Coffin, Full Grave
chapters.summary: Forensics date the soil disturbance to weeks ago: someone reburied the emptied coffin recently, meaning Voss's body was removed long ago—and returned, or moved again, within living memory. Mabel identifies the weekly visitor's car: Crane's. POV: Quentin. Beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: Crane's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Confronted, Judge Crane admits tending the grave—for Voss was his friend, and the coffin was empty because Voss didn't die in 1984. He vanished after the mill deaths, letting the town mourn a saint while he lived as a ghost. POV: Crane flashback framed by Quentin. Beat: pity warring with anger.

chapters.title: Where the Founder Went
chapters.summary: Following Crane's directions, Quentin and Dominic reach a shuttered lake cabin and find evidence Voss lived there until eleven months ago—then find the cabin burned, recent tire tracks, and blood on a hearthstone. POV: Quentin. Beat: hope snatched away.

chapters.title: The Forged Will Explained
chapters.summary: Voss, dying, wrote a true will leaving everything to Dominic and confessing the murders. Someone destroyed it and fabricated the theatrical 'impossible will' to trigger exhumation—exposing the empty coffin and forcing the past open. But who benefits? POV: Quentin. Beat: the mystery inverts.

chapters.title: Mabel's Second Receipt
chapters.summary: Mabel produces a second item she'd withheld: a page torn from Voss's final notebook, mailed to her years ago for safekeeping, naming his killer's motive—the partners' descendants still drawing on laundered mill money. Pike's family. POV: Mabel. Beat: the quiet witness armed at last.

chapters.title: Night at the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Lured by a fake message, Quentin is trapped in the mill by Pike, who confesses: he killed Voss to bury the confession, forged the will's impossibility to control the narrative, and plans an 'accident' like 1984's. Dominic arrives; the bell crashes down between them. POV: Quentin. Beat: climax—fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Closing Arguments
chapters.summary: With the ledger, Crane's testimony, and Pike's recorded confession, Quentin argues the estate case before a packed courtroom, formally reopening the 1984 deaths. Pike is arrested; the will stands. POV: Quentin. Beat: justice delivered without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Three Names Restored
chapters.summary: Halloway buries Voss's recovered remains beside a new memorial bearing the three workers' names—including Quentin's grandfather listed among the responsible. Dominic accepts the inheritance and stays, taking over the mill museum. POV: Dominic. Beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Case Quentin Couldn't Close
chapters.summary: Months later, Quentin hangs a new shingle in Halloway, keeps Mabel's torn notebook page framed above her desk, and takes on a young client nobody else will represent. Some cases, she writes in her journal, you don't close—you carry. POV: Quentin. Beat: resolution as transformation.
